summary: The note compares how different regions manage construction and demolition (C&D) waste, which the global construction industry produces at roughly 35% of the world's waste. It reviews approaches in Europe, Japan, Singapore, Australia, North America and Africa, citing named officials and dated statements. It concludes that culture, policy and technology together determine whether C&D recycling succeeds.
one_line: A comparative survey of national and regional strategies for recycling construction and demolition waste across Europe, Asia-Pacific, North America and Africa.
key_facts: The global construction industry is responsible for producing approximately 35% of the world's waste, per the latest reports post-September 2023.
Germany imposes legal obligations on businesses to minimize waste and prioritize reuse and recycling of construction materials.
Jens Müller, CEO of a leading waste management company in Berlin, said on October 15, 2023 that Germany has achieved a construction waste recycling rate of over 90%.
France uses green public procurement policies requiring contractors to use a certain percentage of recycled materials in projects.
French architect Claude Girard said on November 20, 2023, "We are not just designing buildings; we are engineering a sustainable life cycle of materials."
Tokyo's Metropolitan Government revealed on September 8, 2023 that the capital has seen plummeting landfill rates owing to construction waste recycling initiatives.
Singapore uses an integrated government-private sector approach; Edwin Khoo of the National Environment Agency said on October 3, 2023, "We view C&D waste not as trash, but as a bank of resources."
Australia relies on regional leadership and market-based incentives rather than federal mandates, with Melbourne and Sydney adopting aggressive local strategies.
Melbourne city councilor Samantha Brown said on December 1, 2023 that partnerships are making recycling construction materials cost-effective and environmentally beneficial.
In North America the approach is a patchwork; California has comprehensive C&D regulations requiring a recycling rate above national averages.

British Columbia in Canada has improved recycling infrastructure and public awareness through industry-government collaboration; Vancouver Mayor Robert Kennedy spoke at a virtual summit on September 22, 2023.
Cape Town launched a pilot program, announced by environmental officer Naledi Moyo on September 29, 2023, to turn C&D waste into affordable housing materials.
